strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: The Rust runtime can execute an explicit bounded multi-file replace_file transaction through proposal.apply.
Every transaction item must pass proposal approval, freshness, target hash, path, file kind, symlink, content, and diff gates before writes begin.
Transaction apply results are recorded as bounded ledger evidence with item status and hashes but no raw replacement content or diffs.
Headless callers can request one authorized multi-file workspace mutation and receive a bounded result that distinguishes denied, failed, and applied outcomes.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances controlled_workspace_tools with supporting runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, and headless_autonomous_development.
answers.new_capability: proposal.apply can apply two to five approved replace_file proposals in one explicit bounded transaction request.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Single-file apply cannot enforce transaction-level duplicate path, all-item admission, or multi-file outcome accounting.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Autonomous callers still cannot safely mutate a coherent approved file set without issuing independent applies that can partially diverge.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M13 focused on LLM provider execution; M6 single-file apply lacked multi-file transaction admission and result evidence.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing side-effecting proposal.apply authority is extended with transaction_items.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The result extends the existing apply result with bounded transaction item evidence rather than adding a new report or readiness surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The runtime validates all transaction items before writing and then performs bounded atomic replacements with post-write SHA-256 verification.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Controllers can advance from approved multi-file proposal set to explicit mutation with replay-safe consumed authorization detection.
answers.milestone_progress: Establishes M14's first concrete multi-file workspace mutation capability.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M14.1 changes deterministic current phase manifest. Review must confirm real multi-file replace mutation behavior, not a wrapper or guard-only phase.

exit_criteria: Two approved replace_file proposals can be applied in one explicit transaction and both target files are changed
A stale or mismatched target hash rejects before any transaction file is written and before authorization is consumed
Duplicate, overlapping, protected, symlink, missing, non-UTF8, sensitive, or non-replace transaction items are rejected before writing
Existing single-file replace, create, and delete apply behavior remains compatible

Transaction result and ledger payloads contain bounded item metadata and hashes but no raw content, diffs, patches, absolute paths, canonical paths, stdout, stderr, commands, environment values, API keys, or secrets
No new RPC, diagnostics wrapper, readiness report, digest, history, status wrapper, preview, automatic apply, shell, git, network, or service execution is added
next_phase_candidate_notes: After M14.1 merge, assess whether M14 needs transaction rollback/failure recovery or closeout; do not add a transaction report wrapper.
